section_summary: This section contains State Department docket sheets ('Lists of Papers') cataloguing Military Intelligence Division, Naval Intelligence, and Embassy political reports on Japan from 1930 to 1939, followed by diplomatic records from March through May 1938. Included are telegrams and official paraphrases from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo reporting on Konoe cabinet disagreements regarding China war strategy, a Kobe consular despatch detailing a courageous anti-militarist address by university president Dr. Shinji Tasaki, and a Far Eastern Affairs memorandum evaluating Tokyo Despatch No. 2879. The section concludes with the major portion of Despatch No. 2879, which provides an extensive retrospective analysis of Japan's domestic political crises and its relations with the United States, China, Great Britain, the Soviet Union, Germany, the Netherlands, and Italy before and during the Sino-Japanese hostilities.

subfiles.about: Docket sheet listing Military Intelligence Division reports on Japanese political affairs from March 1932 through December 1939.
subfiles.summary: This multi-page docket list records Military Intelligence Division reports (Sub Nos. 13 to 156) covering internal political developments and foreign relations in Japan between 1932 and 1939. Entries document military attache reports on the Saito, Okada, Hirota, Hayashi, and Konoe cabinets, the February 26 Incident, trials of reactionaries, and anti-communist movements. They also track Japanese military estimates, border clashes with Soviet forces in Manchukuo, the Marco Polo Bridge incident, and ongoing developments in the Second Sino-Japanese War.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Military Intelligence Division Reports on Political Conditions in Japan

subfiles.about: Docket sheet listing Office of Naval Intelligence reports and Naval Attache summaries concerning Japan from 1932 to 1939.
subfiles.summary: Index of Naval Intelligence reports and bi-weekly summaries (Sub Nos. 3-32) on Japan, March 1932 to November 1939, covering naval policy, fleet interviews and Diet debates.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Naval Intelligence Reports on General Conditions in Japan

subfiles.about: Docket sheet listing diplomatic reports on monthly political conditions in Japan from January 1930 to January 1932.
subfiles.summary: Docket list of monthly political reports (Sub Nos. 26-50) from the Tokyo Embassy, February 1930 to February 1932. Page 11 is an alternate exposure of page 10.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Political Reports on Conditions in Japan

subfiles.about: Confidential telegram reporting speculation over an impending Japanese cabinet change and acute divisions regarding military strategy in China.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports a split over China policy: Konoe wants drastic measures against the Nationalist government, War Minister Sugiyama a war of endurance. Parties demand cabinet seats; Saionji to be consulted April 17.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 239 from Tokyo regarding Cabinet Reorganization and Policy on the China Conflict

subfiles.about: State Department paraphrase of Ambassador Grew's confidential telegram detailing Japanese cabinet conflict over China strategy.
subfiles.summary: Paraphrase of Telegram No. 239: Konoe's faction seeks to destroy Chiang Kai-shek's regime, Sugiyama favors attrition; parties want seats; Konoe's resignation averted pending Saionji's advice.
subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Telegram No. 239 from Tokyo regarding Cabinet Disagreement on China Policy

subfiles.about: Internal memorandum highlighting a courageous speech by Dr. Tasaki criticizing Japanese militarism reported by the Kobe consulate.
subfiles.summary: Penfield notes Consul Scott's Kobe despatch on a speech by liberal Dr. Shinji Tasaki, especially his remarks on internationalism and the Imperial Rescript on Education.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Kobe Despatch Reporting Speech of Dr. Tasaki

subfiles.about: Consular despatch transmitting the highlights of an address by Dr. Tasaki expressing regret over military domination and departure from Meiji precepts.
subfiles.summary: Consul Scott reports Dr. Tasaki's March 9, 1938 Kobe speech, lamenting the loss of Meiji military statesmen, saying militarism violates the Rescript on Education, and urging internationalism.
subfiles.title: Despatch reporting Speech of Dr. Tasaki of the Kobe University of Commerce

subfiles.about: Confidential telegram reporting that Japanese cabinet friction has been tided over and the army has conceded to a more vigorous offensive toward Hankow.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Konoe resumed duties, so cabinet differences are temporarily settled; the army conceded to a more aggressive campaign, and a Hankow offensive is expected.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 282 from Tokyo regarding Adjustment of Cabinet Differences and China Operations

subfiles.about: Official paraphrase of Ambassador Grew's telegram concerning the resolution of cabinet friction and military plans for an advance on Hankow.
subfiles.summary: Paraphrase of Telegram No. 282: Konoe resumed duties, cabinet stable, army conceded vigorous prosecution of the China war, Hankow drive probable.
subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Telegram No. 282 from Tokyo regarding Cabinet Adjustment and Drive to Hankow

subfiles.about: Internal memorandum evaluating the Tokyo Embassy's comprehensive review of Japanese foreign and domestic developments since 1937.
subfiles.summary: Ballantine finds Despatch No. 2879, a survey of Japanese foreign and domestic politics from 1937 to April 1938, well written but containing little new.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 2879 Reviewing Japan's Foreign Relations and Domestic Politics

subfiles.about: Comprehensive embassy despatch analyzing Japanese foreign relations with major world powers and domestic political crises from early 1937 through early 1938.
subfiles.summary: This extensive review by Ambassador Grew surveys the outbreak and escalation of the Sino-Japanese War and evaluates Japan's diplomatic relations with the United States, China, Great Britain, the Soviet Union, Germany, the Netherlands, and Italy. It assesses American-Japanese friction following the Panay sinking and Allison incident, severe anti-British agitation, border tensions with the Soviet Union along the Amur River, Germany's ambiguous stance under the Anti-Comintern Pact, and Italy's sudden alignment with Tokyo. The domestic section analyzes the collapse of the Hirota and Hayashi cabinets, army obstruction of General Ugaki, Diet dissolution, and the eventual rise of Prince Konoe to head a non-party national government.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2879: General Review of Events During the Six Months Prior to the Outbreak of Sino-Japanese Hostilities and of Developments Subsequent Thereto
